info.name: OSES — API (Phase 1)
info.description:
Backend endpoints for the OSES API: auth, user + role management, and institute categories.

Auth is COOKIE-BASED: after `Login`, Postman's cookie jar stores `oses_access` + `oses_refresh` (HttpOnly) and sends them automatically on later requests — so `Me`, `Refresh`, admin routes, etc. just work. There are no tokens in the response body.

Set the `baseUrl` variable if your API isn't on http://localhost:3001.

Most admin routes need a Super Admin session: user + role management require the `users.manage` grant, and institute categories require `institute-categories.manage` — both held by Super Admin only, so an Admin or Evaluator gets 403.

The one exception is the `Public` folder, which needs no login at all.

request.description: Verify email + password; sets the HttpOnly auth cookies. Wrong password (6+ chars) → 401; short password → 400; 5 wrong attempts → account locked ~15 min.
Current user (SafeUser). Uses the access cookie. 401 without a session.
Rotate the refresh token and reissue cookies. Replaying an old refresh token → 401 (reuse detected, family revoked).
Change your own password. Revokes ALL sessions — you must log in again afterward.
Revoke the current session and clear cookies.

item.name: Users (Super Admin only)
item.description: Require an authenticated session with the users.manage grant (Super Admin). Others get 403.

request.description: Paginated list of users, newest first. Returns { items, total }, where each item is a SafeUser plus the admin fields 'status' (active/suspended) and 'lastLoginAt'. Query params limit (default 50, max 200) and offset (default 0).
Create a user with a role + temporary password. roleId is one of: role_super_admin, role_admin, role_controller, role_checker, role_institute. Duplicate email → 409. Not a Super Admin → 403.
Set a new temporary password for a user (replaces the emailed reset flow). Revokes their sessions. Put the user id in the :userId path variable.
Activate or suspend an account. status is 'active' or 'suspended'. Suspending revokes the user's sessions immediately.

item.name: Roles (Super Admin only)
item.description: Read-only role catalogue. Requires the users.manage grant (Super Admin); others get 403.

request.description: The 5 system roles with their permission grants (action + scope) — used to populate the role picker on the create-user screen.

item.name: Institute Categories (Super Admin only)
item.description:
The super-admin taxonomy institutes are classified by, plus the dynamic questions each category asks at registration. Requires the institute-categories.manage grant — held by Super Admin only, so an Admin or Evaluator gets 403. Log in first: these use the same HttpOnly cookie as the rest of the API.

These requests keep the {{categoryId}} and {{categoryVersion}} collection variables in step with the server automatically, so you can run List → Update → Update without editing anything by hand.

request.description: Every category, including deactivated ones, each with its active questions and the `version` you must send back when updating. Copy an id into the {{categoryId}} variable.

exec: // Convenience for a fresh start: if no category is selected yet, target the first one.
// Once {{categoryId}} is set this leaves your choice alone.

request.description: One category with its questions. 404 if it does not exist; 400 if the id is not a uuid.

exec: // Keeps {{categoryId}} and {{categoryVersion}} in step with the server, so the next
// Update never fails with 409 just because the version in Postman went stale.

request.description:
Creates the category and its questions together — each question gets a permanent uuid.

Validation: code 1-20 chars (letters/numbers/dash/underscore, case-insensitively unique), name 1-100, at most 50 questions, at most 20 options each.
radio/checkbox/select MUST carry options; text/file must NOT. Unknown fields are rejected.

Duplicate code (even differing only by case) → 409.

exec: // Keeps {{categoryId}} and {{categoryVersion}} in step with the server, so the next
// Update never fails with 409 just because the version in Postman went stale.

request.description:
The category and its question list are saved together, in one transaction.

You do not need to set `version` by hand — List, Get, Create, Update and the status change all capture the current `{{categoryId}}` and `{{categoryVersion}}` from their response. A 409 therefore means a genuine clash: somebody really did save between your read and your write.

`version` is the copy you loaded — send it back and the save applies only while it still matches, so two people editing at once cannot silently overwrite each other.

How the question list is read:
  • a question WITH an id  → updates that stored question, keeping its id (and so every answer already stored against it)
  • a question WITHOUT an id → creates a new one
  • a stored question you omit → removed (retired instead of deleted once it has answers)
  • omit `questions` entirely → the stored list is left completely untouched

Position in the list becomes the display order; ids never change, so reordering is safe.

Answers: 200 · 400 (a question id from another category) · 404 · 409 (someone else saved first — reload and retry, or the code is taken).

exec: // Keeps {{categoryId}} and {{categoryVersion}} in step with the server, so the next
// Update never fails with 409 just because the version in Postman went stale.

request.description:
Sends the state you want rather than toggling, so a double submit is harmless.

Deactivating hides the category from the public registration form while every institute already classified under it keeps working. This is the normal way to withdraw a category — deleting is the rare one.

// Update never fails with 409 just because the version in Postman went stale.

request.description:
Permanent delete; its questions go with it. Allowed only while nothing references the category — once institute registration exists, a category in use answers 409 and you deactivate it instead.

204 on success, 404 if it was already gone.

item.name: Public (no authentication)
item.description: The only routes in the API that need no login. Rate limited, and deliberately narrow.

request.description:
Powers the open institute-registration link, so it answers without any cookie.

Returns ONLY active categories and their active questions, and only these fields: id, code, name, description, questions[id, text, type, required, options]. No version, no isActive, no timestamps — the response is built from an explicit allow-list.

There is deliberately no "get one by id" here, so hidden categories cannot be probed for.

Cache-Control: public, max-age=60. Throttled to 30 requests/minute — exceed it and you get 429.
